Thanks again for the time this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the Dedicated capacity evaluation and integration plan.

Key notes from today:
- Deployment mode: Arcadia is leaning toward Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) to ensure predictable latency for their in-prod ranking pipeline.
- Primary workloads:
  - Re-ranking/embeddings for search (batch embeddings + an online reranker).
  - Structured tool-calling from customer-facing chat (tool calls for DB lookup + search).
- Traffic profile (rough): peak spikes up to ~120 qps for LLM requests, average 25 qps; batch embedding jobs nightly.
- Security: customer prefers mTLS for Private deployments, but open to API-key + VPC for Dedicated in early phases.

Integration/architecture items we need to align on:
1) SDK & auth: confirm whether you'll use our SDK or direct REST for test harness. For Dedicated: recommend mTLS for Private or short-lived API keys with KMS integration for Dedicated. See attached integration_checklist.pdf.
2) Routing & fallbacks: define routing policies (primary dedicated pool, fallback to hosted / smaller model) — will need expected failover SLAs.
3) Structured output & tool calling: we discussed the tool-calling pattern and output schema — we should capture a small contract for the DB lookup tool (input schema + response).
4) Embeddings / reranker: clarify embedding batch sizes and expected dimensionality; we recommend caching strategies and an async rerank queue for high-throughput bursts.
5) Autoscaling & sizing: preliminary numbers below — we'll validate after you share traffic profiles and token lengths. See attached capacity_calc.xlsx.

Preliminary sizing (very conservative):
- Model: open LLM (similar to redwood-7B-quant)
- Avg prompt+response length: 600 tokens
- Target p50 latency: <200ms
- Suggested pool: start with 4 nodes, min_nodes=2, max_nodes=12, target_utilization=65%
- Concurrency guidance: 16 concurrent streams/node for structured output use-cases; use an async queue with 1000 max backlog to smooth spikes.

- Redwood: provide node_config_template.yaml + recommended autoscaler params and queue sizing. (Aditya) — by Fri 03/19.
- Joint: 30m follow-up to review sizing & auth (Marissa to schedule) — propose Wed 03/24.

Thanks Tom — got the staging profile, looks helpful. Quick technical responses and an initial config to help you model cost/throughput. Attached node_config_template.yaml.

1) Estimated per-node throughput (7B quant, mixed seq lengths):
- Concurrent streams/node: ~16 (structured interactive)
- Avg throughput: ~350-450 tokens/sec per node under 16 concurrent streams (your 600-token requests ≈ ~0.6-0.75 reqs/sec per stream)
- So rough requests/sec per node: ~10-12 rps (varying by response length).
- For the conservative peak 120 qps, 10 rps/node -> ~12 active nodes; with target_utilization=65% set max_nodes=18 gives headroom for spikes.

2) Autoscaler / queue pattern:
- Use a two-tier routing approach:
  a) Interactive queue (priority): low-latency path with reserved concurrency slots per node (e.g., 12 slots/node).
  b) Batch/rerank queue (background): async workers that consume capacity when utilization < 70%.
- Implement token-bucket rate-limiter at ingress for bursts and a FIFO priority queue with a small preempt slot for urgent interactive requests.
- Recommend queue backlog sizing: start with 1k total backlog, with per-priority caps (interactive 300, batch 700).

3) Auth & SDK:
- For Dedicated: we support short-lived API keys with KMS + optional mTLS for Private. For your procurement timelines, short-lived keys + VPC peering is easiest to onboard, mTLS can be added during the Private migration.
- SDK: our Node + Python SDKs support automatic key rotation and built-in retry/backoff. I'll share code samples in a follow-up Gist if helpful.

4) Embeddings/reranker ops:
- For nightly batches, recommend batching at 512 and parallelizing across workers. Use prefix caching for repeated queries to reduce online token cost.
- Reranker can be run as a low-latency path if you reserve concurrency; otherwise move to background rerank and update search index asynchronously.

Next steps from engineering side:
- Aditya: provide node_config_template.yaml + suggested autoscaler params (attached) — sent now.
- Arcadia: confirm priority split (interactive vs batch) and provide SRE contact to test connectivity.
